# thoth_tenant_approvers (Resource)

Who may approve held actions on a workspace that has no Slack workspace connected, such as a dedicated deployment. The list is explicit: an empty list means nobody can approve, and there is no all-admins mode. The list is chosen by a signed-in organization admin with recent MFA, so the provider must use `use_thothctl_session` (or an admin bearer token); API keys are refused. Destroying this resource saves an EMPTY list: nobody can approve a held action until a new list is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "thoth" {
  tenant_id            = var.tenant_id
  use_thothctl_session = true # run `thothctl auth login` first; an API key is refused
}
```

```terraform
resource "thoth_tenant_approvers" "this" {
  user_ids = ["user_01HABCDEF", "user_01HGHIJKL"]
}
```

`user_ids` are WorkOS user IDs. Each must belong to a verified, active member of your organization;
the apply fails if one does not. The set replaces the whole list. Saving uses the revision it read, so a
change made by someone else at the same moment is refused rather than overwritten; plan again to see
the current list. Thoth also refuses a person who requested a hold from approving it, so list at least
two people if the same person may raise holds.

**Destroying this resource removes every approver.** It saves an empty list, and then nobody can
approve a held action on the workspace (holds end in `BLOCK` when they time out) until a new list is set.
An empty `user_ids` has the same effect. This matches `thoth_slack_approvals`, whose destroy removes the
reviewers.

This list governs approvals made outside Slack. A workspace with Slack connected keeps using
`thoth_slack_approvals` for approvals made in Slack.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `user_ids` (Set of String) WorkOS user IDs (such as user_01H...) of the people who may approve held actions, at most 50. Each must be a verified, active member of the organization. An empty set allows no one.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform resource identifier (tenant ID).
- `revision` (Number) How many times the list has been saved. A save names the revision it read, so a change made at the same time elsewhere is refused rather than overwritten.
- `updated_at` (String) When the list was last saved (RFC 3339). Empty until the list is first saved.
- `updated_by` (String) The user ID of the admin who last saved the list. Empty until the list is first saved.

## Import

```shell
terraform import thoth_tenant_approvers.this <tenant_id>
```
